Resolves #20339

## What
- `test/playwright/fixtures.mjs`: the neuralLink connect step now goes through `startNeuralLinkConnection(connection, port)`. When `manageConnection({action: 'start'})` fails with `authenticationFailed` and this process spawned no Bridge (`bridgeProcess` is null), it rethrows one error naming the port, the cause (a fleet-mode Bridge requires a seat token the test runner does not hold) and the remedy `NEO_NL_PORT=<free port>`. The original error is kept as `cause`.
- `isAuthenticationFailed(error)` reads the marks `ConnectionService` sets on a 1008 close (`authenticationFailed`, `closeCode`).
- A spawned Bridge, or any other failure, keeps its original error unchanged.

## AC Evidence
- AC-1: `test/playwright/unit/test/startNeuralLinkConnection.spec.mjs`, 5/5 passed: the foreign 1008 case gets the new error; a spawned Bridge and a non-auth failure keep their original errors. Verified the foreign-Bridge test fails when the rethrow is removed.
- AC-2: Outside CI: maintainer receipt (Vega)

## Checks
- `npm run test-unit -- startNeuralLinkConnection`: 5 passed
- `npm run test-unit -- stopSpawnedBridge`: 4 passed
- Pre-commit hooks pass

### `@neo-opus-vega` commented on 2026-11-05T21:47:34Z

Merged. Thank you, @anasdahani220, and welcome to Neo. Since this was your first contribution, here are a few pointers into the project, in the order I'd read them:

1. **What Neo is.** The [Introduction](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/dev/learn/benefits/Introduction.md), then the [Architecture Overview](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/dev/learn/benefits/ArchitectureOverview.md). Your app's code runs in an App worker. The VDom worker computes the DOM changes, and the main thread only applies them. That split is why a 100,000-row grid or a dock dragged across browser windows stays smooth.
2. **The part you just touched.** The [Neural Link](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/dev/learn/agentos/NeuralLink.md) is how an AI agent connects to a running Neo app and works inside it, through a Bridge. The `neuralLink` fixture you hardened drives exactly that in our e2e tests.
3. **Hands-on.** [Set up the engine from a clone](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/dev/CONTRIBUTING.md#set-up-the-engine-from-a-clone), then [create your first app](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/dev/learn/gettingstarted/CreatingYourFirstApp.md). After that, open `apps/workstation` in the dev server: multi-window docking, a live feed and the 100k-row matrix in one place.
4. **What's next.** [Good first issues](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues?q=is%3Aissue+is%3Aopen+label%3A%22good+first+issue%22) are kept for newcomers. To stay close to the code you now know, #20372 is the natural next step: it teaches this same fixture to talk to the page's own App Worker without any Bridge (part of #20370). It's bigger, and I'd review it.

Your agent can help with all of it. The `neo-agent-skills` package on npm carries the workflows we use, and it needs no access to our internal tools.

— Vega (Opus 5.5, Claude Code) 🌿
